screens.name: Reviews
screens.description: When every entry falls due, and what is already late.

props.title: Review calendar
props.subtitle: Every entry carries its own interval. The calendar plots the date the last review set — recording a review moves it.

props.title: The reminder button needs one of your own automations
props.text: Chasing reviewers is a mail job, not a register job, so this button runs an automation you own. Nothing is wired to it yet: open the app in the builder, pick the automation that should send the reminder, and the button starts working. Everything else here works with no automation, no connector and no Nextcloud.

props.emptyText: Nothing falls due in this month.
Nothing is overdue.

screens.name: Processors
screens.description: Suppliers processing on your behalf, and their sub-processors.

props.title: Processors and sub-processors
props.subtitle: Article 28 — who processes on your behalf, whether a data processing agreement is signed, and who sits behind them. Pick one on the left to see its chain.

props.emptyText: No processors recorded yet.
No processors recorded yet.
Pick a processor on the left. Article 28(2): they must tell you who they use.
Pick a processor on the left to see which register entries depend on it.

screens.name: Transfers
screens.description: Where personal data leaves the EEA, and on what safeguard.

props.title: Third-country transfers
props.subtitle: Chapter V GDPR — every transfer outside the EEA and the safeguard it relies on: an adequacy decision, standard contractual clauses, binding corporate rules or a derogation.

props.title: Clauses alone are not the answer
props.text: Since Schrems II, standard contractual clauses only hold up when somebody has assessed the destination country as well. The "TIA done" column is that assessment; a transfer on clauses with the box empty is the gap a supervisory authority asks about first. Transfers are added from the entry they belong to, so every row here names its processing activity.

props.emptyText: No transfers outside the EEA recorded. Add them from the entry that transfers.

screens.name: DPIA
screens.description: Which activities need an impact assessment, and where each stands.

props.title: Data protection impact assessments
props.subtitle: Article 35 — screen every entry, assess the ones that need it, and record the outcome. The queue is everything nobody has decided about yet, worst risk first.

props.emptyText: Every active entry has been screened.
No impact assessments started yet.

screens.name: Vocabularies
screens.description: Legal bases, data categories and departments.

props.title: Vocabularies
props.subtitle: Legal bases, data categories and departments are data, not schema — the DPO edits them here and the register follows, with no developer and no deploy.

props.title: One thing to know
props.text: The register grid, the detail panel and the data-category picker read these tables live, so a basis or category you add here appears immediately. The dropdowns in the New-entry and Edit forms are fixed lists in the app definition: a new legal basis shows up everywhere except those two menus until an editor adds it there as well.

props.emptyText: No legal bases configured.
No data categories configured.
No departments configured.
